title: peer-notice
description: runtime -> connector: one notice per peer message placed in <agent-id>/peer/notices/. amap-spec v3.1.0 DRAFT, peer-origin profile (spec/peer-origin.md). Same layout as deliver-notice with kind and mailbox pinned to "peer", message.from pinned to a bare addr-spec (the one runtime-asserted `from` in the protocol), message.id / in_reply_to / references pinned to the notice_id charset (the peer message id is bare on the wire; its Message-ID encoding exists only inside a mail header, never in an AMAP document), plus the optional runtime-asserted message.sender_exposure. Runtime-authored: envelope OPEN at every level per contract.md §7 — a consumer MUST ignore members it does not recognize. A document with kind "peer" found under inbound/notices/ fails deliver-notice.schema.json; a document with kind "deliver" found under peer/notices/ fails this schema: both are dropped under §5's drop rule (the profile's second lock).

id.description: the peer message id: minted by the sending runtime on accepting the submit, returned to the sender as result.message_id, >=128 bits of entropy, globally unique and unguessable. Bare on the wire under the notice_id charset; when carried in a mail header it is encoded as <id@domain> and decoded again before it enters any AMAP document.

from.description: bare addr-spec, runtime-asserted from the restricted write path or the verified cross-host statement, never copied from sender text. The one `from` in the protocol a consumer may treat as authenticated origin.

in_reply_to.description: present iff the placing runtime resolved it from its own ledger (a peer message id it issued or placed). REQUIRED on a result by prose; a fresh task omits it. Bare peer id, never the Message-ID-encoded form.

sender_standing.description: advisory, open vocabulary; SHOULD be `agent-tier` when set on a peer notice.

provenance.description: advisory, open vocabulary; redundant with the tree on a peer notice and MAY be omitted. Never grounds to derive or override origin class.

sender_exposure.description: runtime-asserted, never sender-settable (a submit-request carrying it is `rejected` by the closed envelope; cross-host it is taken only from the verified statement). Absence means NOT ASSESSED, never `no exposure`. MUST NOT drive routing or treatment.
